chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a woman before whom two witnesses testified that her husband had died, so she married, then her first husband came back.

He عليه السلام said: She is entitled to the dowry because the latter husband lawfully enjoyed her private part. The two witnesses are to be struck with the prescribed punishment and made liable for the dowry because they deceived the man. Then she must observe the ʿiddah and return to her first husband.

key_terms.الْحَدَّ: the prescribed legal punishment applied here for false testimony
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: the dowry owed to the woman due to the valid-looking marital intercourse
key_terms.تَعْتَدُّ: she observes the waiting period (ʿiddah) before returning to her first husband
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا الْأَوَّلُ: her first husband, whose marriage remains operative upon his return
key_terms.شَاهِدَانِ: two witnesses whose testimony led to the mistaken remarriage
key_terms.غَرَّا: they deceived or misled the man through false testimony

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman remarries after witnesses falsely testify that her husband died, and then the first husband returns?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman who remarries after false testimony that her husband has died, only for the first husband to return. It establishes the dowry obligation of the second husband, the liability and punishment of the false witnesses, and the woman's obligation to observe ʿiddah before returning to her first husband.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3334 - Ibrahim ibn Abdul Hamid reported from Abu Basir, who narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a woman for whom two witnesses testified that her husband had died. She then remarried, but later her first husband returned.

Imam (as) said: "The second husband owes her the dowry because he lawfully enjoyed her intimacy. The two witnesses are to be given the prescribed punishment (for false testimony) and held liable for the dowry due to having deceived the man. The woman must observe the waiting period ('iddah) and then return to her first husband."
